q: 1. Fibre boards can be ............
explain: As Per Key in Book option d but As per google Fibre boards have a smooth surface that allows for both painting and distempering for interior finishes.

q: 2. The most commonly used base for timber painting, is ............
explain: White lead is a widely used base for timber painting because it is durable and forms a flexible film that adjusts to the wood's movement.

q: 3. The commonly used base for iron and steel work, is ............
explain: Red lead is the most effective primer base for iron and steel because it provides excellent corrosion resistance.

q: 4. Most commonly used solvent in oil paints, is ............
explain: As Per Book Key of Sunil Sah And India Bix Site Petroleum is correct one  but Turpentine is the most common thinner/solvent used to adjust the consistency of oil-based paints. While other solvents can be used, petroleum is the preferred choice for most artists.So, the given answer is correct.

q: 5. Turpentine oil is used in paints as ............
explain: Turpentine acts as a thinner, reducing the thickness of the paint so it can be spread evenly.

q: 6. Linseed oil is used in paints as ............
explain: Linseed oil is a vehicle (or binder) that holds the pigment in suspension and forms a protective film on the surface.

q: 7. The cracks caused by shrinkage of the exterior surface of the wood exposed to atmosphere are called ............
explain: Wind cracks (or surface checks) occur when the outer layers of wood dry and shrink faster than the inner layers, causing the surface to rupture.

q: 8. The vehicle used in case of enamel paint is usually ...............
explain: Enamel paint is produced by adding pigments to varnish. The varnish acts as the vehicle, giving the paint its characteristic glossy and hard finish.
Lacquer is essentially a spirit varnish consisting of resins dissolved in a volatile solvent like alcohol or nitrocellulose, drying rapidly by evaporation.

q: 10. Monel metal is an alloy of ...............
explain: Monel is a group of nickel alloys, primarily composed of nickel (up to 67%) and copper, with small amounts of iron and other elements.

q: 11. The constituent metal of Bronze alloy are ...............
explain: Bronze is primarily an alloy of copper and tin. If zinc is the primary additive, it is called brass.

q: 12. The constituent metals of the solder are ...............
explain: Soft solder is traditionally an alloy of lead and tin, chosen for its low melting point to join metal surfaces without melting the workpieces.
As per Book key D but as per google Dextrine is produced by the hydrolysis of starch and is commonly used as a water-soluble adhesive for stamps and envelopes.

q: 14. The most important constituent of varnish, is ...............
explain: Resin is the base material of varnish that forms the protective film. Solvents and driers are additives to help with application and drying.

q: 15. The most fire resistant, paints are ...............
explain: Asbestos is naturally fire-resistant; hence paints containing asbestos fibers are used to protect combustible surfaces from fire.

q: 16. To give a brilliant finish the type of varnish used, is ...............
explain: Spirit varnishes (like French polish) dry quickly and provide a very high-gloss, brilliant finish on surfaces like furniture.

q: 17. Creosote oil is used to preserve the wood from ...............
explain: Creosoting is a process where timber is pressure-treated with creosote oil to protect it from fungi (rot) and wood-boring insects (white ants/termites).

q: 18. The commonly used drying oil for oil paints, is ...............
explain: acetate of lead is the most common drying oil because it oxidizes into a tough, transparent, and durable film when exposed to air.

q: 19. French polish is ...............
explain: French polish is a spirit varnish made by dissolving shellac in alcohol, used to give wood a very high-gloss finish.

q: 20. The defect in painting caused due to sliding of one layer of paint over another, is known as ....
explain: Alligatoring occurs when a hard top coat is applied over a soft or wet undercoat, causing the top layer to slide and crack like alligator skin.

q: 21. The varnish is essentially made of ............
explain: Varnish consists of resinous substances (like amber or lac) dissolved in a volatile solvent (like alcohol or turpentine) or oil.

q: 22. The paint which gives illumination during nights is called ............
explain: Fluorescent paints contain pigments that absorb UV light and re-emit it as visible light, providing high visibility or illumination.

q: 23. The most commonly used substance as a vehicle in the oil paints is ............
explain: Linseed oil is the standard vehicle for oil paints because it oxidizes into a tough, transparent, and durable film upon exposure to air.

q: 24. Distemper is a type of ............
explain: Distemper is a traditional water-based paint made from chalk, pigments, and a binder like size or glue, primarily used for interior walls.

q: 25. Turpentine oil is used in paints as ............
explain: Turpentine acts as a thinner or solvent to reduce the viscosity of the paint, making it easier to apply with a brush.

q: 26. Which of the following paint is highly resistant to fire?
explain: Asbestos is a naturally fire-resistant fibrous mineral, making asbestos-based paints suitable for fireproofing applications.

q: 27. Spirit varnish consists of ..........
explain: Spirit varnish is made by dissolving resin (like shellac) in methylated spirits; it dries quickly as the spirit evaporates.

q: 28. The base material for distemper is ..........
explain: Distemper consists of powdered chalk (whiting) as the base, mixed with water and a binder like glue or casein.

q: 29. The liquid medium used in oil paints is .............
explain: Linseed oil is the most common vehicle (binder) used in oil-based paints because it dries into a tough, transparent film.

q: 30. The metallic oxide used in the form of powder in a paint is called .............
explain: The base is a metallic oxide (like white lead or zinc oxide) which is the principal constituent of a paint, making it opaque and durable.

q: 31. The commonly base used in a paint is .............
explain: White lead, zinc oxide, and titanium white are all common bases used depending on the desired finish and exposure conditions.

q: 32. The drier in an oil paint should not be more than ......... (by volume).
explain: Excessive drier can make the paint film brittle and cause it to peel. The standard limit is 10% by volume.

q: 33. Galvanizing means covering iron with a thin coat of .............
explain: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating to iron or steel to prevent rusting.

q: 34. Putty is made up of ............
options: powdered chalk and raw linseed oil
zinc oxide and boiled linseed oil
explain: Glazing putty is prepared by mixing finely powdered chalk (whiting) with raw linseed oil until it reaches a dough-like consistency.

q: 35. Brass is an alloy of ............
explain: Brass is composed of Copper and Zinc. Bronze, by contrast, is primarily Copper and Tin.

q: 36. The best primer used for structural steel work is ............
explain: Red lead is traditionally considered the superior primer for structural steel because it provides excellent corrosion inhibition.

q: 37. The vehicle used in bronze paints is usually ............
explain: Metallic paints like bronze paint typically use a specialized vehicle like nitro-cellulose lacquer to prevent the metallic pigment from tarnishing.

q: 38. The commonly used thinner in oil paints, is ............
explain: Turpentine and Naptha  is the most common thinner used in oil-based paints to adjust the consistency and facilitate easy application.

q: 39. Oil varnish generally consists of ............
explain: Oil varnish is prepared by dissolving hard resins in linseed oil and thinning the mixture with turpentine.

q: 40. Stucco are suitable for ............
explain: Stucco is a type of plaster used for coating exterior walls and surfaces, providing a decorative and protective layer over both stone and brick masonry.
